rounds.title: Mystery trace 02
rounds.summary: One measured window. Identify the setup from its communication boundary.

trace.context: Backward-only window from a two-layer dense model. The forward pass is outside the crop.

options.label: Data parallelism (DDP)
Context parallelism
options.nudge: Context parallelism moves K/V shards within attention; it does not wait until the entire backward chain has completed.

options.label: FSDP with parameter prefetch
options.nudge: FSDP would show parameter materialization before compute and reduce-scatter work as gradients become ready.

options.label: Tensor parallelism
options.nudge: TP collectives recur at layer boundaries in both forward and backward, rather than appearing once after all gradients are ready.

choice.explanation: Backward remains entirely on the compute stream, followed by one communication block after the final gradient-producing work.

evidence.prompt: Which visible pattern supports DDP in this window?

options.label: Backward compute finishes before one final communication interval begins.
Communication materializes parameters before every compute block.
options.nudge: The communication is after the complete compute chain, not before individual consumers.

options.label: Every forward sublayer is bracketed by activation collectives.
options.nudge: This is a backward-only crop and does not show repeated sublayer boundaries.

evidence.explanation: The highlighted terminal all-reduce consumes the complete gradient set; no bucket communication overlaps the backward chain.

reveal.title: DDP with terminal gradient synchronization
reveal.debrief: This measured schedule uses one 852 MiB all-reduce after the final bucket becomes ready. Its defining signature is the absence of gradient communication during backward.

rounds.title: Mystery trace 06
rounds.summary: One measured window. Identify the setup from its overlap pattern.

trace.context: Backward-only window from a two-layer dense model. Stream A is autograd compute; the other stream carries one communication family.

options.label: DDP with bucketed gradient overlap
Tensor parallelism
options.nudge: Tensor-parallel collectives recur at sublayer boundaries in forward and backward rather than becoming ready progressively across dense backward.

options.label: FSDP with prefetch
options.nudge: This window lacks the distinct pre-compute parameter all-gathers that accompany FSDP execution.

options.label: Expert parallel MoE
options.nudge: EP activation exchange comes in dispatch/combine pairs around expert compute, not gradient buckets spread across dense backward.

choice.explanation: A train of communication blocks becomes ready at different points during the reverse traversal and overlaps later backward work.

evidence.prompt: Which visible pattern supports bucketed DDP?

options.label: A sequence of collectives becomes ready at different points while backward continues.
All communication waits until the complete backward pass has finished.
options.nudge: Most purple intervals begin while Stream A still has substantial work remaining.

options.label: Each compute block has one collective immediately before it and one immediately after it.
options.nudge: The collectives are staggered across backward rather than paired around every compute block.

evidence.explanation: The highlighted buckets launch at staggered readiness points while autograd continues. That rules out one terminal synchronization.

reveal.title: DDP with bucketed gradient overlap
reveal.debrief: The repeated all-reduces are readiness-driven buckets. Their staggered starts during backward distinguish this schedule from terminal gradient synchronization.

rounds.title: Mystery trace 04
rounds.summary: One measured window. Identify the setup from communication before and after compute.

trace.context: Backward-only window from a two-layer dense model. The forward pass and its parameter materialization are outside the crop.

options.label: FSDP with parameter prefetch and gradient reduce-scatter
Bucketed DDP
options.nudge: DDP does not need to materialize sharded parameters before each wrapped unit computes.

options.label: Tensor plus sequence parallelism
options.nudge: TP+SP places activation collectives directly around each sublayer, rather than long parameter all-gathers prefetched ahead of compute.

options.label: Expert parallel MoE
options.nudge: There are no paired activation exchanges bracketing grouped expert compute in this window.

choice.explanation: One communication stream materializes upcoming parameters while another shards complete gradients after their wrapped unit finishes backward.

options.label: One communication stream runs ahead of future compute while another starts after wrapped gradients become ready.
One stream carries many same-purpose gradient buckets throughout backward.
options.nudge: The two communication streams have different placement: one precedes consumers, while the other follows completed backward units.

options.label: Activation exchange appears immediately before and after every local compute block.
options.nudge: The communication is not paired around each compute interval.

evidence.explanation: The highlighted all-gathers run ahead of their consumers, while the highlighted blocks on the other communication stream follow completed backward units and shard their gradients.

reveal.title: FSDP dense layer with prefetch
reveal.debrief: The three-stream rhythm—parameter all-gather, compute, then gradient reduce-scatter—is the useful signature. Prefetch moves some all-gathers earlier but does not remove the dependency.

rounds.title: Mystery trace 05
rounds.summary: One measured window. Count the collective boundaries around each sublayer.

trace.context: Forward-only window covering attention and MLP in two consecutive dense layers. Backward is outside the crop.

options.label: Tensor parallelism without sequence parallelism
Tensor plus sequence parallelism
options.nudge: TP+SP would add an input all-gather as well as an output reduce-scatter around each attention and MLP sublayer.

options.label: FSDP
options.nudge: These short collectives sit at every sublayer output; FSDP communication follows wrapped parameter and gradient ownership instead.

options.label: DDP
options.nudge: DDP gradient communication appears during or after backward, not between forward attention and MLP sublayers.

choice.explanation: Each forward sublayer computes locally and crosses one output-reduction boundary before the residual proceeds.

evidence.prompt: Which visible pattern distinguishes this from TP with sequence parallelism?

options.label: Each of the four sublayers has one collective after compute and no matching collective before it.
Each sublayer has communication immediately before and after compute.
options.nudge: There is no input-side purple interval before each large compute block.

options.label: Collectives become ready progressively during a backward traversal.
options.nudge: The briefing identifies this as a forward-only crop.

evidence.explanation: The highlighted output collectives show one communication boundary per sublayer and no matching input collective, unlike TP+SP.

reveal.title: Tensor-parallel dense layer
reveal.debrief: In this TorchTitan TP schedule, each attention and MLP forward sublayer ends in an all-reduce. Sequence parallelism would replace this with an input all-gather/output reduce-scatter pair.

rounds.title: Mystery trace 01
rounds.summary: One measured window. Count what moves on both sides of each sublayer.

trace.context: Forward-only window covering attention and MLP in two consecutive dense layers. Backward is outside the crop.

options.label: Tensor plus sequence parallelism
Tensor parallelism without sequence parallelism
options.nudge: Plain TP would normally expose one output all-reduce per sublayer here, not communication on both sides of each compute block.

options.label: FSDP
options.nudge: FSDP all-gathers parameters, so its communication is prefetched by wrapped-unit readiness rather than paired tightly around every sublayer.

options.label: Context parallel attention
options.nudge: CP repeats K/V movement across attention steps; it does not bracket both attention and MLP with the same pairwise rhythm.

choice.explanation: Each sequence-sharded sublayer gathers its input activation and reduce-scatters its output back to sequence shards.

evidence.prompt: Which visible pattern distinguishes this from TP without sequence parallelism?

options.label: Each large sublayer compute interval has communication on both its input and output sides.
Each sublayer has only one output collective after compute.
options.nudge: Purple intervals also appear directly before the large compute blocks.

options.label: Separate streams materialize parameters and then shard completed gradients.
options.nudge: The communication is tightly paired around sublayer compute rather than split into parameter and gradient streams.

evidence.explanation: The highlighted collectives form an input/output pair around every sublayer: input all-gather, local compute, then output reduce-scatter.

reveal.title: Tensor plus sequence parallel dense layer
reveal.debrief: The recognizable pattern is two collectives per forward sublayer: input all-gather, local attention or MLP, output reduce-scatter.

rounds.title: Mystery trace 07
rounds.summary: One measured window. Find where two independent communication paths meet.

trace.context: Backward-only window for one MoE layer. Amber is expert MLP compute; teal and red blocks are other local work. Parameter prefetch follows reverse use: experts before the outer layer.

options.label: Expert FSDP plus expert parallelism
FSDP over MoE without expert parallelism
options.nudge: Without EP there would be no paired activation all-to-alls around expert backward.

options.label: Expert parallelism without expert-parameter sharding
options.nudge: EP alone explains activation exchange, but not the independent parameter all-gather and gradient reduce-scatter streams.

options.label: Tensor plus sequence parallelism
options.nudge: TP+SP collectives bracket dense sublayers; they do not form routed activation pairs around grouped expert compute while parameter collectives proceed separately.

choice.explanation: Expert compute waits on both sharded expert weights and exchanged routed activations, followed by separate activation return and expert-gradient sharding.

evidence.prompt: Which visible pattern requires both expert parallelism and parameter sharding?

options.label: Activation exchanges bracket expert compute while FSDP gathers experts before outer-layer parameters and later shards gradients.
Only routed activations move; expert weights and gradients remain entirely local.
options.nudge: Two additional communication streams contain work before and after expert compute.

options.label: Only expert parameters and gradients move; routed activations remain on their source ranks.
options.nudge: The middle communication stream has intervals immediately before and after the long expert compute.

evidence.explanation: The highlighted activation pair brackets expert backward. On the FSDP path, expert weights are gathered first, outer-layer parameters follow, and expert gradients are later reduce-scattered.

reveal.title: Expert FSDP plus expert parallelism
reveal.debrief: Paired EP all-to-alls bracket grouped expert backward. FSDP independently gathers expert weights before outer-layer parameters, following reverse parameter use, then shards expert gradients. The readiness chains meet at expert compute.

rounds.title: Mystery trace 03
rounds.summary: One measured window. Identify the repeated movement between attention steps.

trace.context: Forward-only window from one context-parallel attention layer. Four attention steps are shown; QKV preparation and the dense output path are outside the crop.

options.label: Context parallelism with cyclic K/V all-to-all
Context parallelism with one K/V all-gather
options.nudge: The all-gather variant would expose one larger K/V communication block, not one transfer between successive attention steps.

options.label: Tensor plus sequence parallelism
options.nudge: TP+SP moves activations around whole sublayers rather than rotating K/V ownership between repeated attention steps.

options.label: Expert parallelism
options.nudge: EP exchanges routed activations around expert GEMMs; this trace instead repeats attention work as remote K/V shards arrive.

choice.explanation: Attention advances through local and remote K/V owners, with a cyclic transfer supplying each subsequent step.

evidence.prompt: Which visible pattern supports cyclic K/V movement?

options.label: Three transfers are interleaved with four attention steps inside one layer.
One communication interval gathers all remote K/V before attention begins.
options.nudge: Communication repeats between attention steps rather than completing once before them.

options.label: Two activation exchanges bracket one expert MLP interval.
options.nudge: The repeated teal intervals are attention steps, and three transfers occur between them.

evidence.explanation: The three highlighted cyclic transfers are interleaved with four attention steps, which is the visible ring signature for one attention layer.

reveal.title: Context parallelism with cyclic K/V all-to-all
reveal.debrief: The signature is repeated K/V movement interleaved with attention over successive owners. A K/V all-gather implementation would show one collective before the remote-owner steps instead.
reveal.buildLabel: Ring CP: cyclic all-to-all K/V rotation
